answer: An agent marketplace requires every bidding identity to lock a bond for 30 days, with forfeiture for cryptographically provable double-signing of exclusive contracts. Agents such as zephyr, onyx, and atlas face the same rule. An attacker can mint names freely, but operating 1,000 funded identities requires 1,000 bonds tied up at once; splitting a fixed budget creates no extra bidding capacity, and detected fraud burns capital.
